author: Yuri Sidorov (@newstler)
description: Pairs a machine with git.broker, keeps one outbound connection, and when you ask from a PR card creates a worktree and runs your own agent there, headless or in your terminal.

author: ngram
description: Turns a Speaker Deck, SlideShare, Docswell or public Google Slides URL into the ordered list of page images behind it. Pure Ruby with no runtime dependencies and a pluggable HTTP layer, so it runs in slim containers and on ruby.wasm as well as on a normal CRuby.

author: The Pandorga contributors
description: Pandorga is a publishing platform: Jekyll shell, browser content runtime, JSON export pipeline, and Studio editor. Sites declare pages in a registry; the gem supplies templates, gates, and the pandorga CLI.

author: JetRockets
description: CI decides whether a pull request needs a browser run and takes back reviewer requests until an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) has exercised the change in a browser and published what it observed. One command sets a project up.
